metadata.title: Alesvia | The Human Baseline
metadata.description: Alesvia is an emerging Czech institute for the psychological side of artificial intelligence — educating the public, training organizations under the EU AI Act, and preparing therapists for new clinical topics.

hero.title: Human autonomy is the baseline.
hero.description: Alesvia builds research, policy, education, and practical frameworks that help people and institutions stay in control as AI becomes part of daily life.

about.metadata_description: Learn about Alesvia's mission, philosophy, and institutional structure dedicated to preserving human autonomy.
about.label: About Us
about.title: Preserving human autonomy in an automated world.
about.intro: Alesvia exists because automation is outpacing the institutions meant to govern it. We are building the intellectual and structural foundation for a world where technology serves human agency — not the other way around.
about.mission_text: Alesvia is an emerging Czech-founded institutional platform focused on preserving human autonomy in an increasingly automated world. It connects research, policy, education, and practical implementation so that AI strengthens human agency instead of quietly eroding it.
about.philosophy_text: We believe that the most dangerous technologies are not the ones that fail, but the ones that succeed too well — systems so persuasive, so convenient, and so seamlessly integrated that opting out becomes socially or practically impossible. Alesvia exists to ensure that opting out remains a viable choice.
about.origin_text: Alesvia is being established in the Czech Republic as a registered institute (z.ú.) — a legal structure designed for mission-driven organizations that prioritize public benefit over profit; we are preparing for registration. This structure will ensure that our work remains aligned with our principles, not with shareholder expectations.
about.structure_text: A registered institute (z.ú.) under Czech law operates with a statutory board, transparent governance, and a mandate to serve the public interest. Alesvia is currently being established in this form — we are preparing for registration. This is not a startup. It is an institution built to outlast trends and resist capture.

initiatives_index.metadata_description: Explore the four pillars of Alesvia — Unplugged, Academy, Practitioners, and Policy Lab.
initiatives_index.label: Our Work
initiatives_index.title: The four pillars of Alesvia.
initiatives_index.intro: Each pillar speaks to a different audience — the public, organizations, mental health professionals, and policymakers. They share a common institutional foundation, ethical framework, and commitment to the human baseline.

unplugged.metadata_description: Unplugged helps people set healthy boundaries with conversational AI — clearly and without moralizing. AI is a tool, not a relationship.
unplugged.label: Pillar
unplugged.title: Unplugged
unplugged.subtitle: Healthy Boundaries with Conversational AI
unplugged.preview_caption: Preview of the Czech homepage, captured on October 25, 2026. Visit Unplugged for the latest content.
unplugged.intro: Unplugged helps people set healthy boundaries with conversational AI — clearly and without moralizing. AI is a tool, not a relationship.
unplugged.problem_text: AI can feel personal, but it is not a person. Fluent conversation is not the same as a relationship, and an empathetic tone is not evidence of consciousness or understanding. Using AI is okay. Unplugged helps people recognize when AI imitates a friend, partner, or therapist.
unplugged.approach_text: Unplugged develops practical frameworks for individuals, institutions, and policymakers to establish and maintain healthy boundaries with conversational AI systems.
unplugged.principle_friction_desc: We explain how conversational AI works and why it feels so persuasive — without lecturing and without fearmongering.
unplugged.principle_detox_title: AI Is a Tool, Not a Relationship
unplugged.principle_detox_desc: We help people use AI deliberately and toward their own goals — and recognize when a tool starts replacing human contact.
unplugged.principle_boundaries_desc: Clear, enforceable limits on what conversational AI systems should and should not do — from emotional manipulation to data harvesting.
unplugged.cta_text: Unplugged is actively developing its first set of tools and frameworks. If you're a researcher, educator, or policymaker interested in collaborating, we'd like to hear from you.

policy_lab.metadata_description: Alesvia's Policy Lab translates ethical frameworks into actionable legislative and corporate guidelines.
policy_lab.label: Pillar
policy_lab.title: Policy Lab
policy_lab.subtitle: Research & Legislative Advocacy
policy_lab.intro: Technology policy is written by the people in the room. The Policy Lab ensures that the room includes voices focused on human autonomy — not just efficiency, growth, or national competitiveness.
policy_lab.vision_text: To produce research, model legislation, and corporate guidelines that translate abstract ethical principles into enforceable rules. We work at the intersection of technology ethics, regulatory design, and institutional governance.
focus_items: EU AI Act implementation and compliance frameworks
Corporate guidelines for ethical AI deployment
Legislative templates for conversational AI boundaries
Institutional policy toolkits for schools and public bodies
policy_lab.future_text: Two programs will become part of the Policy Lab in the future: a research branch developing science-backed AI literacy, and an independent observatory tracking the real-world impact of AI on human autonomy and society.
policy_lab.cta_text: The Policy Lab is in preparation. Sign up to follow our progress and contribute to our research.

academy.metadata_description: Alesvia Academy — AI literacy and humanly sustainable AI deployment for companies, schools, and public administration, aligned with Article 4 of the EU AI Act.
academy.label: Pillar
academy.title: Academy
academy.subtitle: AI Literacy & Humanly Sustainable AI Deployment
academy.intro: The Academy is preparing AI literacy and humanly sustainable AI deployment for companies, schools, and public administration (including the AI literacy obligation under Article 4 of the EU AI Act). Revenue from these services funds our public-benefit programs.
academy.vision_text: To make AI literacy as fundamental as media literacy — a core competency for informed citizenship and responsible organizations in the 21st century. You cannot set boundaries with systems you do not understand.
programs_items: AI literacy workshops and training for companies and public administration (including the Article 4 EU AI Act obligation)
School curricula on algorithmic literacy and AI awareness
Workshops for educators on integrating digital self-defense into existing courses
Audits of AI tool usage in educational and institutional settings
Public seminars on conversational AI, persuasion, and autonomy
academy.future_text: In the future, the Academy will add a software (SaaS) tool for assessing AI systems — for companies and public administration — and a program for evaluating AI's impact on user autonomy, helping organizations assess their own AI products and services. We also plan to support responsible decision-making around AI investments in the private and public sector.
audiences_items: Companies and organizations deploying AI systems
Secondary and higher education institutions and teacher training programs
academy.cta_text: The Academy is in preparation. We are looking for schools, companies, and institutions willing to pilot our programs and provide feedback. If you represent an organization interested in this topic, get in touch.

practitioners.metadata_description: We are preparing training for psychologists, psychiatrists, and therapists on responsible AI use and its limitations.
practitioners.label: Pillar
practitioners.title: Practitioners
practitioners.subtitle: AI & Mental Health Professional Support
practitioners.intro: We are preparing training for psychologists, psychiatrists, and therapists on responsible AI use and its limitations. Launching the Practitioners pillar depends on securing a clinical lead.
practitioners.problem_text: In the 2025 APA Practitioner Pulse Survey, 56% of responding US psychologists reported using AI at work in the past year; 44% reported never using it at work. The online survey was completed by 1,742 licensed psychologists with doctoral degrees who were actively treating patients. These are self-reported findings from a US sample, not data on Czech therapists or evidence that AI is effective in therapy.
practitioners.problem_source_label: Source: APA and APA Services, Practitioner Pulse Survey (2025), n = 1,742, practicing US psychologists

evidence_items.text: A qualitative study led by Brown University researchers identified ethical risks in the chatbot conversations they evaluated, including inappropriate crisis responses. The analysis covered 137 conversations (110 self-counseling and 27 simulated), seven trained peer counselors, and three licensed clinical psychologists. It was not a clinical efficacy trial or an estimate of how often these risks occur across all users.
evidence_items.source_label: Source: Iftikhar et al., AIES (2025), qualitative analysis of 137 conversations

evidence_items.text: The Delft Digital Ethics Centre at TU Delft held an online workshop on responsible AI for mental health with WHO support on January 29, 2026. WHO reported on it on March 20, 2026. This was an expert discussion with AI governance recommendations, not clinical evidence.
evidence_items.source_label: Source: WHO, March 20, 2026 report on the TU Delft workshop

programs_items: Continuing education programs for mental health professionals on AI literacy
Ethical assessment frameworks for AI tools used in clinical settings
Patient-facing resources: how to talk to your therapist about your AI use
Clinical guidelines for AI-related issues — emotional dependency, parasocial relationships, AI-induced anxiety
Advocacy for regulatory guardrails on AI therapy bots
audiences_items: Their patients — indirectly, through better-informed care
practitioners.cta_text: The Practitioners pillar is in preparation. If you are a mental health professional, researcher, or institution interested in shaping this program, we want to hear from you.

funding.metadata_description: Alesvia's funding model: earned revenue from services, grants, philanthropic partnerships, and infrastructure support — with clear independence rules.
funding.label: Transparency
funding.title: How Alesvia Will Be Funded
funding.intro: Independence requires structural honesty. We publish our funding model because we believe institutional trust is earned through transparency, not branding.
funding.model_text: This is the revenue architecture Alesvia is working toward — none of it is presented as already running. The organization is being established, and we are building its funding from the ground up to resist misaligned incentives: we will not accept funding that compromises our mission, creates conflicts of interest, or introduces pressure to optimize for engagement over human well-being.
funding.source_services_desc: The primary engine and a structural guarantee of independence: revenue from Academy and Practitioners services — AI literacy and training for companies, schools, public administration, and mental health professionals. Any surplus returns to the mission and funds our public-benefit programs.
funding.source_grants_desc: A program accelerator, not operational oxygen. Public and private grants from foundations and government bodies aligned with our mission accelerate specific programs, but the organization does not depend on them.
funding.source_philanthropy_desc: Long-term partnerships with philanthropic organizations and a Founding Circle of founding partners who share our commitment to human autonomy and institutional independence. We also welcome technology companies and investment funds that care about AI being deployed responsibly — under the same independence rules that apply to every donor.
funding.source_infrastructure_desc: Technology credits and tools that lower our operating costs — from cloud infrastructure to software for research and education.
rules_items: We will not accept a donation from an entity whose core product we actively criticize.
Donations are unrestricted — donors do not decide what they are used for.
No single donor will exceed roughly 25% of the organization's annual income.
Donors have no influence over our outputs.
funding.rules_note: This policy will be formally approved by the board after registration.
funding.partners_text: We are currently establishing our first partnerships. If your organization shares our mission, we welcome the conversation.
funding.transparency_text: Once registered as a z.ú., Alesvia will be subject to public reporting requirements. We will go beyond the minimum: our annual reports will include detailed breakdowns of revenue sources, expenditures by pillar, and governance decisions.
funding.cta_text: If your organization is interested in supporting or partnering with Alesvia, we'd like to hear from you.

privacy.metadata_description: Alesvia's privacy policy — how we collect, use, and protect your personal data in compliance with GDPR.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Alesvia respects your privacy. This policy explains what data we collect, why, and how we handle it.

sections.heading: Data Controller
sections.content: Alesvia, an institute (z.ú.) being established in the Czech Republic; we are preparing for registration. Contact: privacy@alesvia.org

sections.heading: What Data We Collect
sections.content: We collect only what is necessary: contact form submissions (name, email, message), basic analytics (anonymized page views), and any data you voluntarily provide. We do not use tracking cookies, behavioral profiling, or third-party advertising scripts.

sections.heading: Legal Basis (GDPR Art. 6)
sections.content: We process data based on: (a) your consent, when you submit a contact form; (b) our legitimate interest in understanding how our site is used, via anonymized analytics; (c) legal obligations, where applicable.

sections.heading: Data Retention
sections.content: Contact form submissions are retained for 12 months unless you request earlier deletion. Anonymized analytics data is retained for 24 months.

sections.heading: Your Rights
sections.content: Under GDPR, you have the right to access, correct, delete, restrict processing of, and port your personal data. You may also withdraw consent at any time. To exercise these rights, contact privacy@alesvia.org.

sections.heading: Third Parties
sections.content: We do not sell, rent, or share your personal data with third parties for marketing purposes. We may use service providers (hosting, email) who process data on our behalf under strict data processing agreements.

sections.heading: Changes to This Policy
sections.content: We will update this policy as needed and note the revision date above. Material changes will be communicated via our website.

items.question: What is Alesvia?
items.answer: Alesvia is an emerging Czech institute for the psychological side of artificial intelligence — educating the public, training organizations under the EU AI Act, and preparing therapists for new clinical topics. Alesvia is being established as a registered institute (z.ú.); we are preparing for registration. Its active program is Unplugged.

items.question: What does Alesvia do?
items.answer: Alesvia builds its work on four pillars: Unplugged (healthy boundaries with conversational AI — active), Academy (AI literacy and humanly sustainable AI deployment for companies, schools, and public administration — in preparation), Practitioners (training psychologists and therapists for the AI era — in preparation), and Policy Lab (translating ethical frameworks into legislation and guidelines — in preparation).

items.question: What is the human baseline?
items.answer: The human baseline is Alesvia's core concept — the non-negotiable set of rights, capacities, and boundaries that must be preserved as automation reshapes society. It represents the minimum standard of human autonomy that technology should not be allowed to erode.

items.question: Where is Alesvia based?
items.answer: Alesvia is being established as a registered institute (z.ú.) with a planned seat in Ostrava, Czech Republic; we are preparing for registration. This legal structure is designed for mission-driven organizations that prioritize public benefit over profit.

items.question: How is Alesvia funded?
items.answer: Alesvia is working toward a model whose primary engine is earned revenue from Academy and Practitioners services — AI literacy and training for companies, schools, and public administration. Revenue from these services funds our public-benefit programs. The model is complemented by grants, philanthropic partnerships, and infrastructure support. The organization will not accept funding that compromises its mission or creates conflicts of interest.

items.question: What is Unplugged?
items.answer: Unplugged helps people set healthy boundaries with conversational AI — clearly and without moralizing. AI is a tool, not a relationship. It is Alesvia's flagship and currently active program.
